blocks.text: JUDGE OF ISRAEL · THE TRIBES OF ISRAEL
Gideon. Three hundred men against Midian; forty years of quiet; he refused the crown.
LED ISRAELi
Not given Not given as years of judging; "the country was in quietness forty years in the days of Gideon"
TRIBE
Manasseh (the Abiezrite family)
IN THE LINE
6th of 15
SCRIPTURE SAYS
“The angel of the LORD greeted him: "The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour.”
PROPHETS
An unnamed prophet
THE TRIBES OF ISRAEL: 15 RULERS MOSES → SAMUEL
THE CYCLE
Forgetting, oppression, a cry, a deliverer, rest
1 · FORGOT GOD "The children of Israel did evil in the sight of the LORD." Judges 6:1

2 · OPPRESSED: MIDIAN, WITH THE AMALEKITES AND "THE CHILDREN OF THE EAST", 7 YEARS For seven years they came up at harvest "as grasshoppers for multitude", and Israel hid in dens and caves. Judges 6:1–5
3 · CRIED OUT "Israel was greatly impoverished because of the Midianites; and the children of Israel cried unto the LORD." Judges 6:6–7
4 · DELIVERED With three hundred men, trumpets and lamps in pitchers, Gideon routed Midian; he then captured its kings beyond the Jordan. Judges 7:16–22 Judges 8:10–12
5 · REST The land had rest 40 years. Judges 8:28
ACCESSION
How Gideon came to power
The angel of the LORD found him threshing wheat in a winepress at Ophrah to hide it from Midian, and sent him: "have not I sent thee?" Judges 6:11–16
Fire from the rock consumed his offering; he built the altar "Jehovah-shalom". Judges 6:19–24
By night he threw down his father's altar of Baal and cut down the grove. Judges 6:25–32
He asked for the sign of the fleece, wet and then dry. Judges 6:36–40
SUCCESSION
Before and after
WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
The angel of the LORD greeted him: "The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour." Judges 6:12
Gideon answered: "my family is poor in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house." Judges 6:15
"The Spirit of the LORD came upon Gideon, and he blew a trumpet." Judges 6:34
Offered a dynasty, he said: "I will not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you: the LORD shall rule over you." Judges 8:22–23
Later Scripture remembers "the day of Midian" and "the slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb". Isaiah 9:4 Isaiah 10:26 Psalms 83:9–11
Samuel names Jerubbaal among Israel's deliverers, and Hebrews among those who acted by faith. 1 Samuel 12:11 Hebrews 11:32
From the Midianite gold he made an ephod at Ophrah: "all Israel went thither a whoring after it: which thing became a snare unto Gideon, and to his house." Judges 8:24–27
After his death Israel made Baal-berith their god and showed no kindness to his house. Judges 8:33–35
EVENTS
Wars, works and turning points
UNDATED IN SCRIPTURE
THE LAND
The places Scripture names
The tribes of Israel · tribe of Manasseh (the Abiezrite family). Only places Scripture names are shown, each where the Atlas puts it.
THE NATION
What the nation did
A prophet reminded Israel of the Exodus: "ye have not obeyed my voice". Judges 6:8–10
The altar of Baal at Ophrah was destroyed, and an altar to the LORD built in its place. Judges 6:25–28
Gideon's ephod became an object Israel "went a whoring after"; after his death they made Baal-berith their god. Judges 8:27 Judges 8:33
PROPHETS
Prophets of the reign
An An unnamed prophet “I am the LORD your God; fear not the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but ye have not obeyed my voice.”
ON THE WORLD STAGE
The powers of the day
MIDIAN, WITH AMALEK AND "THE CHILDREN OF THE EAST"
Zebah, king of Midian · Zalmunna, king of Midian · Oreb, prince of Midian · Zeeb, prince of Midian
DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S OWN NUMBERS
No years given
Seven years under Midian, then forty years of quiet (Judges 6:1, 8:28). No year BC is given.
A priestly garment used to ask the LORD's will
Keil (1865)
Keil holds that "ephod" means the high priest's shoulder-dress with its breastplate, and that Gideon probably wore it to seek revelations; the sin lay in setting up worship outside the sanctuary.[3]
An image or idol
Gesenius and others, as reported by Keil; Moore (1895); Bertheau held it was a golden bull image of the LORD, as reported by Keil
Moore takes "ephod" here as "the specific name of a kind of idol", pointing to the weight of gold and to the editor's phrase "went a whoring after it".[25][3]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 10
Judges 6 Judges 7 Judges 8 Judges 9 1 Samuel 12 2 Samuel 11 Psalms 83 Isaiah 9 Isaiah 10 Hebrews 11
PASSAGES · 8
Judges 6:1–8:35 Judges 9:1–6 1 Samuel 12:11 2 Samuel 11:21 Psalms 83:9–12 Isaiah 9:4 Isaiah 10:26 Hebrews 11:32
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Judges never says that Gideon "judged Israel"; it says the country was quiet forty years "in the days of Gideon" (Judges 8:28).
Scripture does not say what the ephod looked like or how it was used (see the open question).
Abimelech, Gideon's son, "reigned three years over Israel" from Shechem (Judges 9:22) but is not called a judge; he has no page here.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
After he threw down Baal's altar his father called him Jerubbaal; "Jerubbaal, who is Gideon". Judges 6:32 Judges 7:1
From the textThe site's person record also attaches 2 Samuel 11:21, which names "Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth": the same man, with the name formed differently. 2 Samuel 11:21 Judges 9:1
